title: CipherVault: a SOL multisig vault (and the account checks it forgot)
summary: Several owners share a vault. Any owner proposes a payment, others approve, and when the threshold is reached it can be executed. Then audit what the program fails to check.
what: CipherVault is a multisig wallet for SOL. A creator names a group of owners and an approval threshold (for example 2 of 3) and can put SOL into the group's **vault**, a program-owned PDA with no data. Any owner can propose a transfer to a recipient; their own approval is recorded automatically. Other owners approve, and once approvals reach the threshold, execute moves the lamports straight out of the vault. It works end to end on devnet, and its code is also a compact lesson in which account relationships an Anchor program must check itself.
app_note: The fork's own React + Vite app, unchanged apart from the RPC (the fork points at a local validator), the IDL import (the committed IDL in `app/src/anchor/` with this program's address) and the base path. Script: [tests/devnet/patches/ciphervault.py](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/patches/ciphervault.py).

try_steps.do: Set up two Phantom accounts with devnet SOL (Account 1 needs about 1.1 SOL). Copy both addresses.
Open [the app](/dapps/ciphervault/) with Account 1 and connect.

try_steps.see: A `create_multisig` transaction. The card shows 2 of 2, the multisig address and a vault balance of 1 SOL.
ran: New Multisig, 2 of 2, initial balance 1 SOL: the card showed 2 of 2 and vault balance 1 SOL

try_steps.see: A `create_transaction` transaction. The row shows 1/2 approvals (yours is automatic). The amount column shows 0 SOL: it divides lamports by 10⁹ with integer division.

try_steps.do: Switch Phantom to Account 2, reload, open Transactions and press **Approve**.
try_steps.see: An `approval` transaction; the row shows 2/2 and becomes ready.
A `fn_execute` transaction; the row says Executed and the recipient's devnet balance goes up by 0.02 SOL.

diagram:
creator ── create_multisig(threshold, owners[], name, amount) ─▶ Multisig PDA ["multisig", creator, name]
                                                          creator | owners[] | threshold | transaction_count | name | vault | tx_pending
                                                       └▶ Vault PDA ["vault", multisig]  (0 bytes of data, owned by the program, holds the SOL)
owner   ── create_transaction(amount) ─▶ TransactionAccount PDA ["transaction", multisig, transaction_count (u32 LE)]
                                         approval[i] = true for the proposer
owner   ── approval() ─▶ approval[index of signer in owners] = true
anyone  ── fn_execute() ─▶ if approvals ≥ threshold: vault.lamports -= amount; recipient.lamports += amount
accounts: Owners, threshold, counters, the vault's address
PDA `["vault", multisig]`, 0 bytes, owned by the program
PDA `["transaction", multisig, transaction_count as u32 LE]`
Amount, recipient, one approval flag per owner, executed flag

instructions.name: `create_multisig`: owners, threshold, vault
steps: Rejects a repeated owner (`DuplicateOwners`, in Proof) by checking each owner against the rest of the list.

`init` with `space = 0` and seeds `["vault", multisig]` creates an account that holds only lamports and is **owned by this program**. That ownership is what later lets the program subtract lamports from it.
The optional initial amount is moved from the creator into the vault with a System Program transfer.
Note line 17: `#[instruction(..., amount: u64)]` while the handler takes `Option<u64>`. Sending `null` fails with `InstructionDidNotDeserialize` before the handler runs (in Proof).

instructions.name: `create_transaction`: propose and self-approve
steps: The new account's address uses the multisig's `transaction_count` (u32, little-endian), so proposals are numbered 0, 1, 2…
The approval vector has one `false` per owner; the proposer must be an owner (`ProposeNotinOwners`, in Proof) and their slot is set to `true`.
Line 12 compares the vault balance with `transaction_account.amount` **before** line 16 sets it, so it always compares with 0 and never fails. Only execute checks the balance.

instructions.name: `approval`: flip your flag
steps: Finds the signer's index in `multisig.owners` and sets that slot; a non-owner gets `InvalidOwnerError` (in Proof).
Line 23 counts approvals and then does nothing with the result (`{}`): approving never executes.

instructions.name: `fn_execute`: threshold check, then move lamports
steps: Counts `true` flags and requires `threshold <= approvals` (`NotEnoughApproval` with 1 of 2, in Proof).
Requires the vault to hold more than amount + 1 lamport.
`vault.sub_lamports(amount)` / `recipient.add_lamports(amount)`: legal because the program owns the vault; the recipient can be any account.

Sets `executed = true`, but nothing ever **reads** it. Our second execute of the same proposal failed only because `tx_pending` was already 0 (`Underflow`); with another proposal pending it would have paid twice.

innovation.title: a data-less PDA as a SOL vault
innovation.text: The vault is a zero-byte account created by the program at a PDA. It can't sign (no private key), and because the program owns it, the program can debit it with `sub_lamports` without any CPI or signer seeds. Paired with a threshold of approvals stored per proposal, that is the whole multisig.
more: The flip side of "the program can move these lamports" is that the program must prove every account belongs together. Look at `TransactionExecuteContext` (fn_execute.rs lines 42–60) and `ApprovalContext` (approval.rs): the multisig, transaction, vault and recipient accounts have no `seeds`, `has_one` or address constraints tying them to each other. Reading the code, nothing stops a caller from pairing an approved proposal with a different vault or recipient, or approving a proposal through a different multisig in which they are an owner. We did not attack the deployed program; Exercises 1–3 have you add the missing constraints and prove them in a local test.

frontend.title: Create multisig: Anchor resolves the PDAs
steps: The app derives the multisig and vault PDAs for its own use, but passes only `creator` to `.accounts()`: Anchor 0.30 fills in `multi_sig`, `vault` and `system_program` from the seeds in the IDL.

frontend.title: Propose: number the PDA with a 4-byte counter
steps: `transBuffer.writeUInt32LE(transactionCount)` mirrors the program's `transaction_count.to_le_bytes()` on a `u32`, so both sides compute the same address.

frontend.title: Approve and execute
steps: Approve uses `accountsStrict` with three accounts; execute passes the multisig, vault, proposal and recipient taken from the app's own lists. The app passes the right ones; the program just doesn't insist on it.

frontend.title: Two display bugs
steps: `parseInt` on the Initial Balance drops decimals.
`new BN(amount).div(LAMPORTS_PER_SOL)` is integer division: 0.02 SOL shows as 0.

exercises.title: Tie execute's accounts together
steps: In `TransactionExecuteContext`, add `has_one = multisig` support: `#[account(mut, constraint = transaction_account.multisig == multisig.key())]`, `#[account(mut, address = multisig.vault)]` on `vault`, and `#[account(mut, address = transaction_account.reciepient)]` on `reciepient_account`.
`anchor build` and write a local test that calls `fn_execute` on an approved proposal with a different recipient.
exercises.expect: The test now fails with a constraint error; with the original code the same call succeeds and pays the wrong recipient.
exercises.hint: `execute` takes the vault and the proposal as accounts (or remaining accounts) and does not require `proposal.vault == vault.key()`.
exercises.approach: Add that constraint (and any other stored-field links: destination, amount). A proposal created against vault A must then fail if executed against vault B. The recorded successful execute, against its own vault, should still pass.

exercises.title: Execute only once
steps: At the top of `transaction_execute`, add `require!(!transaction_account.executed, ...)` with a new error.
Test: two proposals pending, execute the first twice.
exercises.expect: The second execute fails with your error. Without it, the second call pays again and decrements `tx_pending` for the other proposal.
exercises.hint: Nothing marks a proposal as executed, so the same proposal can be paid more than once while the vault has balance.
exercises.approach: Add `executed: bool` (or close the proposal), set it before the transfer, and `require!(!executed)`. A second execute should fail; the first should still move the amount exactly once, matching the recorded payment.

exercises.title: Approve only through the right multisig
steps: In `ApprovalContext`, add `constraint = transaction.multisig == multisig.key()` on `transaction`.
Test: an owner of multisig X approves a proposal of multisig Y by passing X.
exercises.expect: Rejected after the fix; accepted before (their index in X's owner list flips a flag in Y's proposal).
exercises.hint: `approve` must be sure the proposal belongs to the multisig whose owners you're checking, not 'any proposal plus any multisig'.
exercises.approach: Add `has_one = multisig` (or `constraint = proposal.multisig == multisig.key()`) and that the signer is in that multisig's owner list. Approving with a different multisig's owner set should fail, as the lesson's bug report describes.

exercises.title: Fix the balance check at proposal time
steps: In `create_transaction.rs`, move line 12 below line 16 (or compare with `amount.unwrap_or(0)`).
Propose more SOL than the vault holds.
exercises.expect: Rejected with `NotEnoughSol` at proposal time instead of only failing at execute.
exercises.hint: The vault's balance can change between propose and execute. Checking only at execute (or only at propose) is not enough if you want to reject unaffordable proposals early *and* still be safe at send time.
exercises.approach: Check `vault.lamports() >= amount + rent` at propose (so the UI can fail fast) and again at execute (so a drained vault can't pay). The recorded proposal that was affordable at propose but is no longer should fail at execute after the fix.

exercises.title: Show real amounts in the app
steps: In `TransactionTable.tsx` line 96, display `tx.amount / LAMPORTS_PER_SOL` as a number (or `toFixed(4)`); in `CreateMultisigDialog.tsx` use `parseFloat`.
exercises.expect: The 0.02 SOL proposal shows 0.02, and an initial balance of 0.5 SOL is accepted.
exercises.hint: The app has the same class of display bug PulseFund has: a BN shown from the wrong field, or in lamports without a label.
exercises.approach: Find where the UI formats the threshold, the amount and the vault balance. Show SOL with a clear unit, from the full BN value, and compare against the amounts in the Proof transactions.

not_covered: The full create → propose → approve → execute cycle was clicked through with two wallets. Not exercised: the SPL-token option in the dialog (the program does nothing with it). The missing account constraints described in section 4 come from reading the code; we did not attempt them against the deployed program. Lists use getProgramAccounts on the public RPC and can be slow.
objectives: Walk a multisig: propose, approve, execute when the threshold is reached.
Find the account checks that are missing at `execute` and at `approve`, each proven on devnet.
Fix the leftover-accounts path so a proposal can only move funds from its own vault, and only once.
prereqs: Phantom on devnet and about 0.1 SOL. A second wallet is useful for the 'other owner' steps.
[Friendstake](/lessons/friendstake/) and [UniProof](/lessons/chinesepowered-solana-cypherpunk/): you have practised spotting a missing `has_one`. This lesson is that idea at execute time.

build.note: The program crate is named `cipher-valut` (the typo is in the repo). Tests: `tests/cipher-valut.ts`.
